previous.quote: A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements. The aim of this study was to test the specificity of a manual approach bias for high-calorie food in grasp movements compared to low-calorie food and neutral objects of different complexity, namely, simple balls and geometrically more complex office tools.

decision.reason: Both complete original reports are available:2016grasp/ward food-versus-ball findings include faster food collection, whereas2021adds office-tool complexity controls and reports a slower food collection contrast with faster earlier movement stages. The current abstract describes an earlier VR/manual approach-bias study broadly, uses office controls and finds faster high-calorie grasp/collection, but its full body/in-text attribution remains unavailable. Task resemblance does not alone exclude a later follow-up from the closest chain or establish whether both reported findings are retested. Thus allocation relative to existing1827remains an actual current-body/finding-attribution limit after original-source attempts. No second original from DOI/year alone. The latest expert p<.001claim for Max onset is not adopted: the verified original context distinguishes onset/contact tests and collection. All raw reasons remain unchanged.
